record.title: Relore combines repository decision history with current-code search; reported retrieval gains remain narrow
record.summary: A September 21, 2026 Hugging Face community article and the public relore repository describe a tool that indexes issue and pull-request history with author and trust metadata, then joins that history to current-code search in a maintained clone. Its project-authored, model-judged retrieval evaluation reports Recall@10 rising from 0.938 to 1.000 for 48 Transformers failure queries after query expansion, and from 0.375 to 0.475 for 40 precedent queries. The larger pooled rationale result is contaminated by same-thread answer leakage; the leak-free rationale slices are only 7 and 9 examples. In one author-reported Transformers case, relore found two existing fix threads and the agent avoided writing another patch; a code-browsing overview reportedly used about 5% of the tokens needed to read a whole file. These results support bounded accounts of retrieval and one field case, not a general reduction in duplicate work, better patches or higher coding-agent productivity.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A public Apache-2.0 repository describes relore, which indexes issue and pull-request history with author/trust metadata and serves current-code search against a working clone.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Project-authored, model-judged retrieval results report Recall@10 for a Transformers sample of 48 failure queries rising from 0.938 to 1.000 with query expansion, and 40 precedent queries rising from 0.375 to 0.475; the same report identifies contamination in pooled rationale results and supplies leak-free rationale slices of 7 and 9 examples.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The repository evaluation does not establish a general reduction in duplicate work, improved patch success, or end-to-end coding-agent productivity across repositories.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In one reported Transformers case, relore found two existing fix threads and the agent avoided writing another patch; a separate author-reported code-browsing comparison says one file overview used roughly 5% of the tokens needed to read the whole file.

evidence_gaps.description: The retrieval benchmark and the single reported field case have not been independently reproduced or audited.
The reported retrieval metrics do not measure reduced duplicate work, patch success or end-to-end agent task outcomes.
The leak-free rationale slices are small (7 and 9 examples), and the larger pooled rationale slice includes same-thread answer leakage.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported retrieval behavior holds, repository history indexed by authorship, trust tier and code location could change how coding agents recover design decisions and in-flight work. Its current evidence is a project-authored benchmark on limited, model-judged slices and does not establish end-to-end task improvement.
limitations: The reported benchmark is project-authored and model-judged; no independent reproduction or human-label audit was performed.
The Transformers benchmark uses 48 failure, 40 precedent and 51 pooled rationale queries; leak-free rationale subsets contain only 7 and 9 examples.
The pooled rationale result is contaminated because a reviewer finding can appear in the same thread as the answer; the repository separates leak-free subsets and notes the limitation.
The project reports one field case in which an agent avoided a duplicate patch and one token-use comparison, not a controlled measurement of repeated task success or general agent productivity.
The index is per repository and may lag later GitHub changes by its polling interval; cross-repository search and second-fresh answers are outside its design.

technical.claimed_result: The repository reports improved Recall@10 from query expansion in limited model-judged retrieval samples: Transformers failure queries (48 examples) rise from 0.938 to 1.000 and precedent queries (40 examples) from 0.375 to 0.475. The report flags pooled rationale leakage and gives separate leak-free rationale samples of 7 and 9. In one reported field case, `inflight` found two existing fix threads and avoided a third patch; an author-reported code overview used roughly 5% of whole-file tokens.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public repository and Apache-2.0 license are accessible; README and evaluation docs describe the tool and benchmark. The measurements are project-reported, not independently reproduced. The Hugging Face article reports one Transformers case and the token comparison; these are author-reported observations, not controlled general-effect measurements.
technical.mechanism: Index historical issue/PR discussion at comment level with authorship and trust tier; extract files, symbols, tests and commit signals; serve structured queries alongside code search against a maintained repository clone.
technical.regime: One Transformers repository history benchmark with 48 failure queries, 40 precedent queries and 51 pooled rationale queries, plus small leak-free rationale slices from Transformers (7) and bot-review repositories (9). Labels are model-judged. The project also describes one author-reported case with six agents investigating the same Transformers bug. The field report describes one Transformers issue; it is not a repeated-task benchmark.
technical.reproducibility: The public repository includes code and evaluation documentation. The Hugging Face article reports one field case. The README, evaluation docs and article were inspected, but code and benchmark results were not independently reproduced.
technical.strongest_baseline: The project compares relore retrieval with GitHub search and grep on the same query windows. Results vary by query type; rationale outcomes are sensitive to answer leakage, and the leak-free subsets are small.

brief.title: Relore combines repository decision history with current-code search; reported retrieval gains remain narrow
brief.why_it_matters: Coding agents can repeat work when they miss an in-flight change or the rationale behind existing code. Relore combines historical discussion, authorship and trust metadata with current-code search, and reports retrieval gains on limited benchmark slices. The evaluation also exposes same-thread leakage and small leak-free samples; it does not establish better patches or general productivity.
